feature: The Sunfish's daggerboard is one board through the deck: the part above the deck, its gasket and the splash guard line up with the board below (they had been 6 cm forward of it), and the tip is rounded instead of cut square.
features: board_mid_x (build_fleet, Sunfish only): the above-deck board, the slot's gasket and the splash guard centred on the underwater board's chord, the above-deck part its full chord
board() (Sunfish only): the tip rounded, 80 mm at the leading edge and 25 mm at the trailing edge, the flat between them at the physics' draft

the tip keeps the board's full 19 mm (each tip section's thickness ratio from the full chord), its faces wound outward, and the above-deck board's eased top edge inset so it is the board's own edge, its ends capped inside the wood
references: Round 2's blind reviewers (the daggerboard and rudder as plain slabs); class photos of the Sunfish's wooden board (one flat board, rounded tip).
moves_ok_note: The board's parts above the deck move 6 cm aft to sit on the board below; the splash guard (fittings) moves with the trunk.
mac_note: No game code changes. The Mac rebakes and reimports the Sunfish.
findings: Blind A/B: 3 of 3 reviewers (realism, boatbuilder, 3D artist) picked the rounded, aligned board, each by a small margin.

QA: the alignment, draft (-0.890 m), thickness (slab 19.0 mm, foil 19.2 mm) and clearances hold; nothing else moved (the fittings' 14 vertices at the ratchet are the weld picking other survivors, under 0.01 mm). Fixed after QA: the tip had thinned to 10.8 mm (now 19.1 mm to the bottom), the rounding was sampled away from the tip (now clustered toward it, 6 points on the trailing radius), the foil's faces were wound inward (now outward), the eased top edge stood 10 mm proud of the board's edges with open ends.

Reviewers' notes for later: no slot or fairing where the board leaves the hull bottom; the blunt bow and forefoot step (the physics hull's end); the rudder a flat plate on a boxy head; the board's handle cap reads tall. The ILCA's board is 6 cm out of line the same way (not in this slice).
